note: One defect, two signatures depending on build config. The root cause (confirmed by reading lib/HLSL/DxilCondenseResources.cpp, function UpdateResourceSymbols, introduced in dc3ad5efe/2018-02-05, long predating this issue and predating SM 6.6/ResourceDescriptorHeap) is `DXASSERT(GV->user_empty(), "else resource not lowered")`: when a statically-bound resource global is used *before* being reassigned to a dynamic ResourceDescriptorHeap handle, the static handle's uses do not get lowered away by the time this pass runs, so GV still has a user. Under NDEBUG (Release/shipped release binaries) the assert compiles out and execution falls through to unconditionally replace the resource's DXIL-visible symbol with `undef` while leaving GV (which still has a real user) in the module -- that stale, now-unreferenced-by-metadata GV is exactly what the validator later reports as "External declaration ... is unused", matching the issue verbatim. Under a Debug build (our ground truth, asserts compiled in) the DXASSERT traps first, before the validator ever runs, producing an internal compiler error (0x80000003, `!(GV->user_empty())`, DxilCondenseResources.cpp:1984) instead of the validation text. Matching only the regex would score every Debug-build probe (including ground truth) as a clean run and erase the defect; matching only internal_failure would score every historical Release probe (including the one that produced the reporter's exact quoted text) as a crash instead of the reported symptom. The regex clause is anchored to the specific validator wording quoted in the issue, not a bare nonzero-exit, since ordinary diagnosed E_FAIL failures are common and unrelated to this defect.
